evidence.explanation: The performance-check skill requires window-dependent claims to be measured in a real window rather than inferred from headless results. The new runner adds days 41–55 as a comparison window, while its comparison always requests rendered summaries; the analyzer rejects summaries without two map draws. The probe overloads days 40–54, and the map viewport increments its draw count only after a map draw.

findings.description: `finish_runtime_display_frame()` returns publication ID 0 unless vision succeeds and the commit has a `day_tail` whose day matches `_climate_writeback_applied_day`, and `queue()` replaces even an earlier pinned publication with that 0. This occurs when graph authority is ready but climate authority is not yet granted or is deliberately retained on the main thread, as well as when vision fails; deferred map reads then reject the ID, leaving the map stale until another commit arrives, potentially indefinitely in a paused world, while daily results can still be delivered.

evidence.explanation: Graph readiness is marked independently of the climate authority grant, and the control report exposes separate `authority_ready` and `climate_worker_authoritative` values. The adapter skips climate writeback when climate authority is false but still takes the whole-graph path and calls `finish_runtime_display_frame(true)`; its pin condition then returns 0 when the climate writeback day does not match, and a failed vision snapshot also prevents the pin. `queue()` stores that 0 over the previous publication ID, and `read_runtime_map_lut_frame()` rejects IDs at or below 0 before texture publication.

findings.description: In `_publish_worker_map`, a failed `read_runtime_map_lut_frame` returns false and calls `push_error` only when `needs_recovery` is false. Once one failure has set recovery, every later rejection (map mismatch, generation mismatch, column size, allocation) returns with no log, and the map stays stale.
findings.title: Repeated map read failures are not logged
